related_questions.question: How do you treat ecthyma gangrenosum?
related_questions.snippet: Treatment / Management Initial empiric therapy includes antipseudomonal beta-lactams (piperacillin/tazobactam), cephalosporins (cefepime), fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin), and carbapenems (imipenem). Combination therapy is recommended in high-risk individuals, such as those with neutropenia and septic shock.

related_questions.question: How to diagnose ecthyma gangrenosum?
related_questions.snippet: Diagnosis generally requires confirmation by additional tests, including blood cultures, cultures and gram stain of the wound, and skin biopsies. Gram stain of fluid from the wound shows many gram-negative, rod-shaped bacteria in the case of pseudomonal ecthyma gangrenosum.

text_blocks.snippet: Ecthyma is typically diagnosed through a physical examination, where a doctor can identify the characteristic skin lesions, and potentially through lab tests like wound cultures or skin biopsies.
snippet_highlighted_words: through a physical examination, where a doctor can identify the characteristic skin lesions, and potentially through lab tests like wound cultures or skin biopsies

list.title: Physical Examination:
list.snippet: Doctors can often diagnose ecthyma simply by looking at the skin lesions, which are typically ulcers with a thick, crusty covering.

list.title: Wound Culture:
list.snippet: If the diagnosis is uncertain or if the infection is severe, a sample of fluid from the lesion may be sent to a lab for culture and sensitivity testing. This helps identify the specific bacteria causing the infection and determine the best antibiotic treatment.

list.title: Skin Biopsy:
list.snippet: In some cases, a skin biopsy may be necessary to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other conditions that can mimic ecthyma.

list.title: Differential Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Doctors will also consider other conditions that can cause similar skin lesions, such as ecthyma gangrenosum, rickettsial infections, or insect bites.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, the diagnosis of ecthyma combines:

list.snippet: Clinical assessment: Observing the skin lesions and their characteristics.
Laboratory tests: In some cases, to confirm the infection and guide treatment.
Ruling out other possibilities: Considering other potential causes of the skin lesions.
